original: A public compatibility standard can benefit consumers and firms by placing products on a common technical interface. Yet agreement about the desirability of compatibility need not produce a common standard. Governments care about the profits of domestic producers as well as the benefits to consumers, and these interests may differ across countries. An additional institutional obstacle is easy to overlook: a proposal cannot pass a vote unless someone with the legal right to place it on the agenda chooses to do so. A standard may have enough supporters to win, but no authorized sponsor willing to introduce it.
proposed: The governments of two countries may favor replacing a private regional standard even when its founding firms want to retain it. Whether that majority can act depends on who may introduce the public alternative. We ask whether firms can preserve a regional equilibrium by adjusting their earlier investments when proposal access expands.
reason: Generic opening delays the private/government conflict; identify the investment question immediately.

original: Our first result identifies a sharp constitutional threshold in an explicit region of economic primitives. When one or two affirmative national votes are sufficient, \emph{public standardization is the only pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibrium terminal outcome if and only if at least two governments hold independent proposal rights}. With a sole proposal holder, the other two countries can sustain a privately developed bilateral standard, and the public standard is also supported by an equilibrium. Unanimity preserves privately developed regional equilibria regardless of how proposal rights are distributed. The threshold thus concerns the set of \emph{equilibrium outcomes}, not the uniqueness of each initial technological choice. The analysis does not rule out mixed-strategy equilibria.
proposed: Under a prescribed national proposal and voting rule, we establish a threshold for pure-SPE terminal outcomes on an explicit parameter region. When one or two affirmative votes suffice, a public interface is the only terminal standard type in every pure SPE if and only if at least two governments may independently propose it. A sole outsider proposer and unanimity can sustain bilateral regional equilibria. The result covers all legal continuous private investments; it does not identify a unique initial investment vector.
reason: Separate the reduced political rule, domain and terminal-outcome quantifier.

original: Why does this institutional threshold extend beyond voting over an assumed private standard? In a three-country polity, any two authorized proposers intersect every two-government majority. The observation is elementary. But an arbitrary private technology profile need not yield two favorable votes. Some heterogeneous private standards can indeed make particular governments oppose a public interface. Our central equilibrium task is therefore to rule out private investment profiles that would both evade the public vote \emph{and} survive a firm's incentive to deviate. With two developers, excessive unilateral compatibility or commonality capital can be reduced without changing the common pair technology; at higher commonality choices, a smaller design adjustment raises private profit while leaving political nonintervention intact. With three developers, surviving private profiles must have ties in their maximal design attributes; careful analysis of the remaining asymmetric cases shows that two national governments weakly support the public mandate. Only after these private-investment restrictions are established does the institutional majority-intersection argument complete the result. Our equilibrium claim is consequently stronger than an ex-post vote calculation at a symmetric regional benchmark.
proposed: The set-intersection argument behind this threshold is elementary: any two proposal holders intersect every two-country majority. The substantive equilibrium step is to show that firms cannot sustain a no-intervention design with insufficient effective political support. Redundant investment reductions and global payoff inequalities establish this step for heterogeneous two- and three-developer histories.
reason: Keep the proof idea; move the long case description to the equilibrium section.

proposed: Compatibility capacity determines the demand benefit that a compatible pair can obtain. The second attribute is a design stock that changes product substitution: it makes products within a two-firm cohort closer substitutes while separating that cohort from the remaining producer. These effects are assumed reduced-form demand primitives. The restriction that design commonality cannot exceed compatibility capacity defines the feasible investment triangle.

original: At date 2, governments observe the entire vector of initial technology choices. A constitution consists of a nonempty \emph{agenda set} \(\calA\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\) and a \emph{YES quorum} \(r\in\{1,2,3\}\). Every government in \(\calA\) may independently introduce the legally available public mandate; a mandate passes if at least \(r\) governments vote YES. A government always proposes an implementable mandate if it weakly gains from doing so, and votes YES when its national welfare under the mandate weakly exceeds the status quo. These tie rules are maintained throughout. Since the possibility of enactment is common knowledge, this deterministic continuation may be represented by a sequence of individually available public motions and national votes; the legal proposal right does not confer bargaining power over the technical content.
proposed: After observing private investments, the institution applies a prescribed proposal and voting rule. A government supports the fixed public motion when its national welfare gain is nonnegative, and an eligible supporter introduces it whenever it can pass. The mandate is enacted exactly when the number of supporters meets the quorum and at least one supporter has proposal eligibility. Firms anticipate this continuation rule when choosing investments. Our pure-SPE statements refer to this reduced game; unrestricted simultaneous voting can support additional continuations.
reason: A substantive institutional clarification, not a change secretly made to the manuscript.

proposed: At the privately optimal regional design, both founding governments gain from a public mandate even though each founding firm earns more from retaining the private standard. Consumer benefits account for that divergence. The outsider government instead loses because its domestic firm must incur new setup and compatibility costs. The signs are uniform over the stated optimal-design enclosure. Proposal eligibility determines whether these national preferences can lead to enactment.

original:
The distinction is economically transparent. A privately developed regional standard uses the commonality stock \(a_R^*>0\) to separate a compatible insider pair from a third producer. If the public standard is chosen at the outset, none of that commonality capital needs to be built. If the government instead imposes it after the region has developed the alternative design, the same expenditure has already been made and cannot be recovered. The public outcome then requires firms to abandon the attribute that generated the regional differentiation advantage. The opportunity cost of that abandoned design is
\(\phi(\aR)^2\) across the two regional founders. The two world-welfare comparisons differ by exactly that amount.
proposed: The commonality expenditure is already sunk in both alternatives considered after regional investment, so it cancels from that policy comparison. It is incurred only along the regional initial investment path. The ex-ante and ex-post cutoffs therefore differ by the two founders' historical commonality costs. Endogenous design choice determines the size of this wedge, not the accounting reason that it is positive.

original: The same institutional reform has no unconditional efficiency ranking. The nonmember's national veto, the world-welfare effect of retrofitting after private expenditure is sunk, and the welfare ranking of alternative initial public and private investment paths have three distinct cutoffs. Their ordered difference shows why desirable public standardization at the outset can coexist with an undesirable retrofit after private investment. A rule that produces a unique public equilibrium can also remove a privately developed equilibrium with higher ex-ante world welfare.
proposed: The institutional result does not provide an unconditional efficiency ranking. A nonmember's vote, a retrofit of an installed regional standard, and a comparison of two initial investment paths involve different thresholds. Wider proposal access can remove a feasible regional equilibrium that has higher ex-ante welfare than the NNN-to-public path. Without an equilibrium-selection rule, this does not identify the realized welfare effect of reform.

original:
Consider two identical open founders \(O(c,a)\) and an undeveloped outsider. Write
\[
 b=\gamma_0+\kappa a-vc,\quad d=\gamma_0-\eta a,
 \quad z=1+\rho c,\quad D=2m(2m+b)-2d^2.
\]
The two symmetric insider quantities \(x\) and the outsider quantity \(y\) solve
\[
 \begin{bmatrix}2m+b&d\\ 2d&2m\end{bmatrix}
 \begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}
 =
 \begin{bmatrix}z\\1\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Inverting the matrix gives
\begin{equation}
 x=\frac{2mz-d}{D},\qquad
 y=\frac{2m+b-2dz}{D},\qquad D>0.
 \label{eq:app-xy}
\end{equation}
The gross net-of-stock-but-pre-setup profit of a founder is
\[
 F(c,a;\eta)=3m x(c,a,\eta)^2-\frac{\phi}{2}(c^2+a^2).
\]
At fixed \(a\) we have the exact comparative-static identity
\[
 \frac{\partial x}{\partial c}
 =\frac{2m(\rho+vx)}{D}>0,
\quad
 \frac{\partial F}{\partial c}
 =6m x\frac{\partial x}{\partial c}-\phi c.
\]
The second derivative expression alone does not establish a global optimum. A uniform rational inequality uses a conservative positive lower bound on \(x\,\partial x/\partial c\) and confirms \(\partial F/\partial c>0\) on the full feasible triangle for \(\eta\in[.10,.14]\); hence the optimal pair design has \(c=1\).
proposed: The sign of the first derivative must be established uniformly before the compatibility boundary can be declared globally optimal. The rational lower-bound argument verifies this sign over the full feasible triangle.
reason: The source refers to a second derivative expression immediately after displaying the first derivative of F with respect to c.
